notes:
Look and language
- Colour schemes: Dark (the old Default), Dim (replaces High readability), Light, or Follow the system, in Settings > Help & diagnostics > Colour scheme. Footage, flag colours and the timeline keep their true colours in every scheme.
- Cut Valet speaks Spanish: pick Language / Idioma in Settings or on the first-run wizard. The Projects page, the new project form, ingest, Settings, the wizard and the tour are translated so far; the rest follows. Chat answers and AI-written text follow your language too.
- On a Mac, the app menu says "Settings..." like the rest of the app.

Naming and renaming
- Name patterns for clips, camera bins and files, in Settings > Folders: new tokens, a typed {Token:format} syntax and a short code per camera.
- Optionally rename the card copy by your file pattern while it copies, and rename files already in a project (Rename files... on a clip's menu, or Settings > Folders). Every rename is journaled: Undo from the Activity log, and a crash mid-rename puts the originals back.

Catalog
- Much faster on big archives (tested at 109,000 clips): tiles first, results stream in, Cancel really stops a search, and a local poster cache (capped at 2 GB) keeps scrolling smooth.
- Full-text search over names, descriptions, tags and transcripts, plus a "Looks like" switch beside the search box (off by default).
- A new side rail: one Drives tree, Library, Collections and a Pick list, with dates you can drill into. Open a clip into a full-size loupe view inside the page.
- Searchable exposure: ISO, aperture, shutter, white balance and picture profile.
- Exclude folders from an archive index (junk folders are excluded by default).

Analysis
- Snapshot descriptions, the search index and (on an NVIDIA card) transcription and on-screen text reading run in a separate helper process by default (Settings > Tech stack > Run GPU models in a helper process). On a long archive run, Snapshot descriptions were about 17% faster per clip, and the window stalled less than half as often. If the helper cannot start, the work runs inside Cut Valet as before.
- Analysis runs at below-normal priority so Resolve always comes first. New Lite mode (Settings > Analysis) caps analysis at a share of the CPU and lifts the cap while you are away.
- Temporal descriptions now cover the whole clip, head included, and decode each clip once instead of once per frame.
- A paired audio recorder is found by its own start time, and the clip is transcribed from the recorder's WAV instead of the camera's scratch track.
- Translate transcripts: a new analysis job (off by default) and a Show translations switch in the inspector. Descriptions, metadata and plans can be written in your language.
- Best-Take Picker: takes are ranked per retake group, with a Review takes strip and one-click Promote.
- Claude Haiku 4.5 is a cloud choice for descriptions.
- The queue's spinners keep turning while analysis is busy, and many reads that could freeze the window for a moment now happen in the background.
- New: Footage > Re-describe Clips with Gaps... re-describes only the clips whose Temporal descriptions cover part of the clip, when you choose to. It shows how many and the time (or the dollars, for a cloud engine) first; Cancel queues nothing.
- Opening a project no longer asks whether to re-describe clips whose older Temporal descriptions cover only part of the clip.

Projects and Resolve
- Workspace defaults: save a workspace's settings as the starting point for its new projects (Projects page).
- Follow Resolve's project: an optional setting that switches Cut Valet when you switch projects in Resolve, without the click.
- Colour management: Cut Valet asks once per project before changing Resolve's colour science, and never changes it unattended.
- Set Resolve's location by hand if automatic discovery cannot find it.
- A notice at import when a project mixes frame rates. 23.976 and 24 (and 29.97 and 30) count as the same rate, and Cut Valet follows Resolve's choice.
- Clips with no camera profile get a Pick camera profile... button.
- Speed ramps and photo flashes render in Resolve, and high-frame-rate clips are cut in the frames Resolve uses.

Fixes
- On a Mac, one file seen under two letter cases no longer becomes two clips; Maintenance can merge any that already exist.
- An exFAT drive is no longer offered as a camera card by its format and size alone.
- ARRIRAW (.arx) and RAW stills (.srw, .pef, .x3f, .gpr) count as clips, and a WAV's length is read from the file.
- "Analysis finished" no longer appears while work is still owed, and a clip with no picture stops being re-queued on every open.
- The auto-cut filler-word list is editable, and the AI and Analysis sections of Settings have Reset to defaults.

Deliver
- YouTube: before uploading, Cut Valet asks if your channel already has a video with the same title; if that check cannot run, it says so.
- Social Distribute is gone. Your own AI agent (Claude Code or Codex, with Cut Valet's MCP tools) publishes and writes captions better with your own context. Saved platform tokens and past distribute records stay where they are.
- New tool, Your workflow (Tools, Publishing): open the export's folder, copy a ready-to-paste hand-off for your AI agent (the file, its title, description, tags and cover), or name a script that runs after every export with the file's path and a small JSON of the same details.
- Wrap the project and Teach the assistant are back on the Deliver list: the first step you add brings them with it.
- Deliver everything and the YouTube card's own Upload now send exactly the same file, cover, title, description, tags, schedule and captions.
- The render of the YouTube 4K preset (named ..._4K_H264) is now recognised as the cut's YouTube render and master, so Deliver no longer falls back to whatever the watch folder last loaded.
- The Deliver page is hidden now, on its way out: publish through Your workflow or your own AI agent. To keep using it for now, turn on Settings > Help & diagnostics > Show the Deliver page (under Show advanced); it comes back straight away. Exports, the export watcher and Run after each export work either way, and Your workflow's hand-off now carries the title, description and tags you saved even when the Deliver page was never opened.

Assistants (MCP)
- Claude desktop and Claude Code connect more reliably: the connect-time reply is about 2 KB instead of 31 KB (the full guide is still one call away), and sign-in checks get a clean "not found".
- cutvalet-mcp: a small connector program, so a Claude session that starts before Cut Valet still has its tools.
- run_jobs now analyses clips from an indexed archive in place (describe, motion, stability, previews, search index, no copy) instead of skipping them as "not in the catalog" when another project is open, and says where each clip was filed; the archive browser's Analyse works on search results across archives too.
- An assistant can Start up and Stand down without a click at the machine: both follow your autonomy setting like any other change (at Just drive they just run; at Halfway or Minimal with "Ask me before an assistant connected over MCP changes anything" on, they still ask), headless too. New tool stand_down hands the machine to the editor before a render. A stand-down that you or an assistant made is never lifted by Cut Valet's own idle timer.
- New tools: the Catalog's Pick list (show, add, remove, clear), list_collections and run_collection, sync_media_pool, and archive excluded folders. make_stringout and create_timeline_document can start from the Pick list, and search_archive gains phrase search, Looks like and the rail's sets.
- Agents read a clip's timed Temporal events (what_happens) first.
moved: Tools > Your workflow, or bring the page back in Settings > Help & diagnostics > Show the Deliver page
added: Colour schemes: Dark, Dim, Light or Follow the system (Settings > Help & diagnostics).
Rename files already in a project, with Undo (Settings > Folders).
